---
title: "Trump tariffs 2.0 Part II"
description: "Two weeks of tariff whiplash: North American duties imposed then rolled back, followed by new steel, aluminium, and reciprocal-tariff measures."
date: "2025-03-06"
categories: [trade-wars]
---

Tracking two weeks of announcements through February 2025: Trump first
imposed 25% tariffs on Canada and Mexico and 10% on China (citing fentanyl),
then reversed the North American tariffs after negotiations while keeping
China's in place. By mid-February he expanded the protectionist push further
— 25% steel and aluminium tariffs effective March 4, plus an executive order
on reciprocal tariffs targeting VAT regimes and non-tariff barriers in Japan,
India, and the EU. Throughout, the consistent finding is that these tariffs
reduce trade volumes, lower output, and diminish welfare for everyone
involved.

**Originally published on Substack**, March 6, 2025.
